description: Matches the speed tier a managed vellum.ai assistant actually runs, so the memory/background call sites are compared against the production model instead of a Claude stand-in. Captured from `assistant inference callsites list --json` on a live platform assistant (2026-08-03): there, IS_PLATFORM routes llm.defaultProvider through `vellum`, and every call site resolves to one of two models - `balanced` = gpt-5.6-luna and `cost-optimized` = accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash. An eval hatch is OFF-platform, so the SAME two profile names resolve down the BYOK anthropic column to claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-haiku-4-5. That is not a tuning difference: memoryRetrospective ran Haiku in evals and deepseek-v4-flash in production, which is the largest confound in the procedural-memory results. This profile pins the 22 cost-optimized call sites to the exact production model via Fireworks BYOK. The balanced sites are deliberately left on Claude: the assistant's `openai` provider speaks the Responses API, which the egress recorder cannot parse, so pinning them to gpt-5.6-luna would report their spend as $0 - trading a known model gap for a silent cost gap. Fireworks is on RECORDED_USAGE_HOSTS, so everything this profile changes stays cost-accounted. Requires FIREWORKS_API_KEY in the runner environment. Also forces memory.v3.live=true (vellum-assistant#39847); that step is a harmless no-op once the fix ships in the published sandbox image.
setup: assistant inference providers connections create fireworks-personal --provider fireworks --auth api_key --credential credential/fireworks/api_key

assistant inference profiles create prod-speed --provider fireworks --model accounts/fireworks/models/deepseek-v4-flash --connection fireworks-personal --effort none --max-tokens 8192 --thinking false --label "Prod Speed"
